subject: Error message about NAs for SEM

messages.author: 16613620be8fa776
messages.subject: Error message about NAs for SEM
parts:
Dear all,
I recently tried to fit this model:

Model <- '

Latentvar =~ A + B + C+ D + E

F ~~ A+ B + C+  D + E +Latentvar

C ~~ D

Latentvar ~~1*Latentvar

'

fit_model <- sem(Model, vars, estimator= "MLMV", mimic="Mplus")


All variables A:F are manifest variables. My supervisor, who uses Mplus, manages to get the model to work, but I do not in lavaan; I keep getting " Error in tmp[cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx])] <- lavpartable$free[idx] : NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments"
I read the 2016 post about this error message, but my R is up to date, I don't see any typos, and there are no missing data.

Does anyone have any advice?
Kind regards,
Tara

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Error message about NAs for SEM
parts:
On 6/23/23 15:20, 'Tara P' via lavaan wrote:
> Dear all,
> I recently tried to fit this model:
>
> Model <- '
>
> Latentvar =~ A + B + C+ D + E
>
> F ~~ A+ B + C+D + E +Latentvar

>
> C ~~ D
>
> Latentvar ~~1*Latentvar
>
> '

This model does not not make sense to me: an observed variable 'F' is
correlated with both the factor AND its indicators?

To make this work with the default LISREL representation, you must
'upgrade' all the indicators (A-E) to single-indicator latent variables
manually.

An alternative is to use the RAM representation:

fit_model <- sem(Model, vars, estimator= "MLMV", representation = "RAM")

Yves.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Error message about NAs for SEM
parts:
You don't mention observed variable F at all now. The number of observed variables has been reduced from 6 to 5, so the number of unique elements in the observed variable covariance matrix has been reduced by 6--6 * (6 + 1) / 2 vs 5 * (5 + 1) / 2. You previously gave F saturated relationships with all the other variables, using up all of those extra degrees of freedom. If you want F in the model but uncorrelated with the other variables, then mention it:

F ~~ F

That should get you more degrees of freedom and a worse fit.

There should be a 7th parameter when F is included--the variance of F. But maybe there was an automatic scaling constraint that took care of that.
On Tue, Jun 27, 2023 at 6:58 AM 'Tara P' via lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:

One last question:
I decided to kick out the " Latentvar ~~1*Latentvar " part at the top. When I run that model, I get the same chi², df, and p-value for the chi² as when I run the baseline model

Model <- '

Latentvar =~ A + B + C+ D + E

C ~~ D

'

So the only difference is whether manifest variable F is correlated to the rest, or not. How can that be? I am very confused.

Thanks for your help in advance!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Error message about NAs for SEM
parts:
You were using up all the information gained by including F to estimate parameters related to F. The chi-square test tests constraints. Free parameters do not constrain the solution. Maybe you are thinking of regression, where the "F test" is a function of variance explained, so that adding parameters changes the "F statistic". (I use quote marks to distinguish the F test from your observed variable F.) Remember that regression models are essentially saturated--there are no net constraints--so the test of fit in factor-based SEM would not be appropriate in regression.
Here, there was no difference in overall discrepancy between (1) the model that included F but consumed all of the extra information associated with F and (2) the model that excluded F.
